metadata.concept_name: ZeroFizz Sugar-Free Carbonated Beverage - Customer Journey Map
metadata.product_name: ZeroFizz Sugar-Free Carbonated Beverage - Customer Journey Map
metadata.objective: Map the end-to-end customer journey for a health-conscious adult 18-35 with a sugar-free carbonated beverage — from first awareness (TikTok ad, a friend's can at a picnic, an endcap at Trader Joe's) through curiosity and research (ingredient-label scrutiny, Reddit and creator reviews, sweetener identity comparison), first single-can trial (where, when, what occasion), first-taste reaction and aftertaste verdict, second-can decision and 12-pack commitment, integration into weekly rituals (2pm desk slump, post-workout, rooftop-bar alcohol substitute), social use in peer settings where others are cutting back, and the evaluation moments that drive recommendation, switching to Celsius or Olipop, or outright abandonment after an ingredient controversy or price increase. Capture touchpoints, friction (availability drops, sweetener distrust, lifestyle-marketing skepticism), and moments of delight (a flavor discovery, a clean energy boost, a Dry-January social win) at each stage.

turns.question: I'd love to hear about your relationship with sugar-free drinks — so think back to when you first started noticing them or trying them out, and just walk me through how that whole thing unfolded for you, from that first moment you became aware of them all the way to where you are now with them.
turns.response: Honestly, I don't remember a specific moment where I was like "oh, sugar-free drinks exist." They were just kind of... there at some point. I started grabbing them more in my twenties when I got a bit more conscious about calories and stuff, mostly diet sodas at first. Then I realized they all taste kinda weird to me — that artificial sweetener thing — so I'd go back to regular for a while, then feel bad about the sugar, then try diet again. It's been pretty back and forth honestly.

turns.question: When you'd go back to regular drinks after the artificial sweetener taste bothered you, what made you decide to switch back?
turns.response: Honestly I just got tired of the aftertaste. Like after a few weeks it stops bothering you, but then you have a regular soda and remember what it actually tastes like, and going back feels kind of pointless if I'm not enjoying it as much.
